solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lay out papers, receiving pound: great!

indicators.note: whatever receives something takes it inside itself, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to lay out money is to spend it
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
identity papers are ID

explanation.surface: Someone spreads out the newspapers, takes in a pound coin and is delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay out' looks like arranging the papers, but it means paying out money; 'papers' are identity documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Both work as an enthusiastic exclamation of approval, meaning excellent or wonderful.

clue.text: Smoothing round knot, not missing floorboards

indicators.note: the second word tells us the first must be absent, so those three letters drop out
to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: planing wood smooths it
the word with its last three letters, n-o-t, removed leaves just its first letter

explanation.surface: A carpenter smooths around a knot in the wood so no floorboards are missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not missing' reads as 'none absent', but it tells you to take NOT out of KNOT, leaving K, which PLANING then wraps round.
explanation.definitionFit: Planking is a collective noun for planks laid as flooring or decking, so it names a set of boards.

clue.text: Fan wobbled badly in alternating motion

indicators.note: something done badly is out of order, so the preceding letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An electric fan shakes about as it oscillates from side to side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobbled' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'badly' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the tide going out and coming back, a recurring movement back and forth.

clue.text: Much of the universe not seen to be important after nightfall

definitions.text: Much of the universe not seen

indicators.note: coming after means following on, so one piece is placed behind the other

parts.note: nightfall is dark, as in 'home before dark'
things that matter are important

explanation.surface: Astronomers find most of the cosmos invisible, yet it becomes important once night falls.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads in reverse order, with the second piece named first. The definition is a long description rather than a single synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists posit an invisible substance making up most of the cosmos's mass, detected only through its gravitational pull.

clue.text: Loved to hold me up and put down

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: doted, as in doted on, means loved

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone adored was lifted up, then dropped and humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' only reverses the pronoun, which in a down clue then reads upward; it sits after the first letter of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone down can mean to lower them in rank or status, which is a demotion.

clue.text: A slander upset assembly

indicators.note: to upset is to overturn, and in a down clue an overturned word reads bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
slinging mud is slander

explanation.surface: A defamatory remark disrupts a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: A MUD is reversed whole. 'upset' looks like it describes the assembly but it works on the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duma is the elected lower house of Russia's parliament, a legislative body.

clue.text: Ancient kingdom, not all in South Africa

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: SA is the standard abbreviation for South Africa
something not all of a thing is only part of it

explanation.surface: An old realm was only partly located in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all in' looks like a hidden-word signal, but 'not all' is a word meaning a portion, which goes inside the country's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek city-state was ruled by two hereditary kings and is famed for its military culture.

clue.text: Next US prosecutor turns judge with a little money

indicators.note: turning round makes something face the other way, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a District Attorney is an American prosecutor
J is the abbreviation for judge
taken as written
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: An American prosecutor next approaches a judge with a small bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Next' looks like it belongs to the story, as in 'next, the prosecutor', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Things side by side are neighbouring or contiguous, lying beside one another.

clue.text: In full gear he commonly told a joke

parts.note: dropping the H, as in casual speech, turns 'he' into 'e
to quip is to make a witty remark

explanation.surface: Fully kitted out, a man cracked a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' signals the dropped aitch of casual British speech, so 'he' loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fitted out with all the necessary kit, tools or clothing is ready, outfitted.

clue.text: Climb awkwardly missing large raised curve

indicators.note: what is missing is absent, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: to clamber is to climb clumsily, using hands and feet
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A clumsy climber loses footing on a big humped slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' looks like an anagram signal, but 'Climb awkwardly' together is the verb CLAMBER, which then loses L.
explanation.definitionFit: Camber is the slight convex arch built into a road surface so rain drains off to the sides.

clue.text: Throaty sound on apple heard, a bird

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it, so the first-named piece comes second
what is heard reaches the ear, so the spelling is chosen to match a spoken word

parts.note: a cooker is a cooking apple, like a Bramley
a burr is a rough, rolled R pronounced in the throat
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone makes a gurgling noise over an apple, which sounds like a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A cooker is British for a cooking apple, sour fruit meant for pies rather than eating raw. 'a' looks like the article before 'bird' but supplies the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This large Australian kingfisher is famous for its loud call resembling human laughter.

clue.text: Thoughtful character

definitions.meaning: second meaning: sort or type, as in 'of that character'

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a description of a person, but each is a separate meaning of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means caring and considerate; as a noun it means a sort, class or nature.

clue.text: Do better to speak formally after email fails

indicators.note: something that fails breaks down, so its letters fall into a new order
coming after means following on, so one piece is placed behind the other

parts.note: rearranged
to orate is to give a formal speech

explanation.surface: Advice to improve your communication: talk properly when email lets you down.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled EMAIL comes first and ORATE follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is to improve or make something better; it can also mean to become better.

clue.text: Subordinate working as detective, talent almost wasted

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined, so its letters are broken up and rearranged
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a machine that is in is on, working
the Criminal Investigation Department is the British police detective branch
cut short to five letters, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A junior officer serving as a detective is squandering most of their ability.
explanation.walkthrough: TALENT loses its last T before being jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incidental is minor or secondary, happening as a side matter rather than being central.

clue.text: Put back in control over situation, died

indicators.note: in a down clue, being over something means sitting above it, so that piece comes first

parts.note: a rein is a means of control, as in 'keep a tight rein'
a state of affairs is a situation
d. is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone restored to power in a crisis then passed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back in control' reads like one phrase, but the definition ends at 'back'; 'in' joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate someone is to restore them to a former position, so they are returned to it.

clue.text: Father lacking in delicacy and nimbleness

indicators.note: something lacking is without a part, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: delicacy, in the sense of being easily broken, is fragility
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A priest who is neither delicate nor quick on his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: FR is removed from the front of FRAGILITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nimble means moving quickly and lightly, the quality of physical deftness.

clue.text: Swearing about regular instalments of satire not being easy to get

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: verbal abuse is swearing

indicators.note: instalments arriving at regular intervals means taking every other letter

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Cursing about a satirical magazine's serial whose jokes are hard to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' is used in its informal sense of understand, as in 'I don't get it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstruse ideas are obscure and difficult to understand, so they are hard to grasp.

clue.text: Most painful infection just starting in a breast

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the breast is the chest

indicators.note: only starting means we keep just the opening letter

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: An infection beginning in the breast is causing the greatest pain.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside CHEST after its second letter, with A in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Achy means sore; the superlative describes whatever aches the most, hurting worst of all.

clue.text: Peter to install something reliable for party

parts.note: in old criminal slang, a peter is a safe
to seat a part is to fit it in place

explanation.surface: A man named Peter is putting in something dependable for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a name but is safecracker slang. 'party' is a political party, not a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: In British politics, a safe seat is a constituency a political party can count on winning at every election.

clue.text: Excel, almost certain to involve a teammate

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: sure, cut short
you pass the ball to bring a teammate into play

explanation.surface: Spreadsheet advice: you are nearly bound to need a colleague's help with Excel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excel' looks like the Microsoft program, but it is the plain verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel and to surpass both mean to outdo, going beyond others or a standard.

clue.text: Who's suggested an outdoor arena?

parts.note: surface reading: asking which person put forward an idea
setter's reading: the answer, split as a word for display plus a word meaning crushed, is an instruction to jumble a display word, producing these four letters

explanation.surface: A question about who has put forward an open-air venue.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: split the answer into two words, and the second, meaning milled or crushed, acts as an anagram signal on the first, giving the clue's opening word.
explanation.definitionFit: A showground is an open field where agricultural shows and fairs are held.

clue.text: Solemn and old, want to keep lucid in the head

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a wish is a want

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: A grave elderly person hoping to stay mentally sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside WISH after the W, and O comes first. 'and old' looks like part of the definition, but the definition is 'Solemn' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are seen as grave and wise-looking, so an owlish person has a serious, studious air.

clue.text: One endless hoo-ha about devout Muslim

indicators.note: with no end, the final letter is cut off
turning about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
a fuss without its final S

explanation.surface: Someone is making an unending fuss about a pious believer.
explanation.walkthrough: I and the shortened FUSS are put together, then the whole string is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sufis are Islamic mystics devoted to seeking closeness to God through prayer and asceticism.

clue.text: One turning over dough is very rich and secure

parts.note: 'rolling in it' means very rich
to pin something is to fasten it

explanation.surface: A shrewd investor turning over money becomes wealthy and financially safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dough' is slang for money, so the definition looks like an investor; it is the baker's tool, which literally turns over dough as it rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolling pin is a cylindrical kitchen utensil rolled across pastry to flatten it.

clue.text: Type of film that doesn't use infrared?

parts.note: using none of something is having no
IR is the abbreviation for infrared

explanation.surface: A question about which kind of movie avoids infrared light.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful reading: a film with no IR. It also suggests camera film, though the answer is a cinema genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Film noir is a genre of dark, cynical crime dramas, typically shot in shadowy black and white.

clue.text: Finally without appeal, he had paid a percentage

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: last letter
'it' is sex appeal, an old slang sense
he'd, the contraction, without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: With no chance of appeal left, a man has handed over a share of his income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without appeal' reads like a legal phrase, but 'without' only supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe is a tenth of income given to the church, so to tithe is to pay that fraction.

clue.text: Supports us with cheers during lapses

indicators.note: something happening during another falls within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: moral lapses are sins
taken as written
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: Fans keep a team going by cheering whenever it slips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheers' looks like applause, but in Britain it is also a casual thank-you, as is TA.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to keep it going or bear its weight, which is what supporting means.

clue.text: Anti-communist union lacks a Republican firmness

indicators.note: what something lacks it does not have, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Solidarity was the Polish trade union that challenged communist rule in the 1980s
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A trade union opposed to communism is short of the resolve of a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: A and R both come out of the middle of SOLIDARITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Solidity is the quality of being solid, hard and stable, with no give.
